item.title: 2026-08-22 - Canada tariff war, Iran off-ramp, havens jump
item.description: Canada tariff standoff flipped overnight from very close to a deal to a 50 percent levy on about $20bn of goods, with Carney threatening to retaliate dollar for dollar. Iran signalled an off-ramp days before Trumps toughest-ever sanctions land, while investors piled into gold and Bitcoin on doubts the Treasury can cap long-term yields.

item.title: 2026-08-21 - Bond rescue stalls, China rebuffs Iran push, data-center revolt
item.description: The Treasury buyback faltered on day two, one analyst likening it to paying your mortgage with your credit card, and equities sold off as AI-capex borrowing keeps yields elevated. China publicly rebuffed Washington on squeezing Iran, the data-centre backlash turned electoral in New York and crossed into Alberta, and AT and T is now routing about 40 percent of its internal AI work to cheaper open models.

item.title: 2026-08-20 - mRNA cancer vaccine, US debt tops $40T, data-center backlash
item.description: The first Phase 3 win for a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine, with AI picking the neoantigen targets and Moderna up about 177 percent, set against a data-centre backlash that around 70 percent of Americans now share. US debt crossed $40T amid a global bond rout, with AI infrastructure issuance itself part of what is lifting yields, while Trump swapped Iran talks for economic asphyxiation.

item.title: 2026-08-19 - Canada tariff pause, OpenAI freezes Astra, Iran talks collapse
item.description: Trump pauses the 50 percent Canada tariff with two hours to spare; OpenAI halts training on Astra over critical cyber risk while Anthropic argues the opposite; Iran talks collapse as the Hormuz squeeze tightens.

item.description: Nvidia backstops OpenAI's 10GW Ohio build; Anthropic's run rate passes OpenAI ahead of a fall IPO; Meta's child-safety trial opens with up to $1.4T at stake.

item.title: 2026-08-17 - Iran truce expires, Kushner meets Hamas, Chinese AI surges
item.description: Kushner meets Hamas to revive a Gaza ceasefire even as Israel strikes Lebanon, while the U.S. cuts joint drills with South Korea and China presses its advantage. Alibabas Qwen becomes the worlds most-downloaded model family, the A2A agent protocol goes neutral with Microsoft backing, and the grid regulators data-centre deadline lands.

item.title: 2026-08-16 - Iran plane-swap, $3.7T infra gap, Arctic eclipse
item.description: A deliberately short Sunday edition - only 1440s weekly roundup published. U.S. infrastructure spending is set to hit $5.4T this decade yet still leaves a $3.7T repair gap, the physical backdrop to the AI build-out, plus a lightly-sourced report that Trump secretly switched planes in Turkey amid an Iranian missile threat.

item.title: 2026-08-15 - Mangione guilty plea, Iran-Hormuz standoff, Colombia quake
item.description: A lighter weekend edition: Mangione pleads guilty federally with the state double-jeopardy fight now the thing to watch, and U.S. violent crime posts its largest annual decline on record. China opens its first Arctic Ice Silk Road lane to Europe, and Colombia's quake toll reaches at least 281.

item.title: 2026-08-14 - US-China tariff clash, AI's price war, Iran squeeze
item.description: Washington accuses Beijing of a Great Transshipment Scam and hits drones with 100% tariffs, while signalling an open-ended economic and naval squeeze on Iran. Google, OpenAI and DeepSeek all ship cheaper and faster models within 24 hours, and Flock curbs its plate-reader dragnet after a stalking scandal.

item.title: 2026-08-13 - Grok 4.6 = GPT-5.6, Anthropic's $3T IPO, Canada tariff crunch
item.description: Grok 4.6 reaches GPT-5.6-class quality at a fraction of the cost per task, while Anthropic's October IPO chatter balloons toward $2-3T alongside a ~$6B Decart deal. Cooling U.S. inflation takes a September Fed hike off the table, and Canada-U.S. trade talks stall days before the Aug 19 tariff wave.
